questions.knowledgeNote: Add entrywise; matching shapes is the validity condition for +/-.
questions.question: Q1(a). If A = [[1,2],[3,5]] and B = [[4,-1],[2,3]], compute A+B, A-B and 2A+3B.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.9 Ex 9.1 Q1(a); book p248 = PDF p275 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Addition needs identical order: B is 2x2, C is 2x3, so only A+B and A-B exist.
questions.question: Q1(b). If A = [[1,2],[3,5]], B = [[4,-1],[2,3]] and C = [[1,2,3],[0,1,4]], compute the following, if possible: (i) A+B (ii) A-B (iii) A+C.
questions.solution: (i) A+B = [[5,1],[5,8]]. (ii) A-B = [[-3,3],[1,2]]. (iii) A+C is NOT possible: A is 2x2 while C is 2x3, and addition requires identical order.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.9 Ex 9.1 Q1(b); book p248 = PDF p275 (vision read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Scalar multiple acts on every entry; check each entry against the key.
questions.question: Q2. Compute: (i) 2[[1,4],[2,5]] (ii) (1/2)[[1,4],[2,5]] (iii) 3[[4,0],[2,-3]].

questions.knowledgeNote: AB multiplies rows of A by columns of B; BA has different entries: the classic non-commutativity example.
questions.question: Q3. If A = [[1,3],[2,5]] and B = [[-2,0],[1,4]], show that AB != BA.

questions.knowledgeNote: AC is 2x2 via inner dimension 3; CA is blocked (3-wide times 2-tall).
questions.question: Q4. If A = [[1,0,-1],[3,2,1]] and C = [[1,2],[0,3],[-2,5]], show that AC != CA (one side may fail to exist).
